# First mixed deposit capture

Public read-only responses captured on 2026-09-11 from new peers 0/1 and pinned reference peers 2/3 after the same first deposit was claimed. All four returned the same populated Wallet and claimed discovery, including native Bitcoin outpoint strings. This directly observes the populated reference Wallet string representation, which earlier evidence had only inferred. All four report 55 Mint recovery records and no pending Bitcoin chain. Client denomination counts are a sanitized CLI count report, not independently verified note secrets/signatures or guardian issuance counters. No tokens, invites, private keys or client database files are retained. No daemon/Core/driver mutation was performed to capture this evidence.

Earlier receipt stderr warned that chain_id was unavailable on new peers and later reported output_info_slice connections closed. Receipt subsequently progressed; this capture does not determine that warning's root cause. This is first-deposit evidence, not completion of consolidation/reissue/withdrawal/recovery gates.

First-claim accounting: 100,000,000 msat Wallet assets minus 99,261,952 msat reported client notes leaves 738,048 msat. The captured receive_fee quote is 632 sat; the supplied mining fee has not been decoded from the accepted transaction. **If the supplied fee equals that quote**, the difference decomposes into 632,000 msat withheld first-deposit mining fee, 100,000 msat Wallet input fee, 55 × 100 msat Mint output fees, and 548 msat excess input. The 548 msat excess is therefore conditional, not an independently observed transaction value. The first claim creates no consolidation; any supplied mining fee withheld remains in Wallet assets (WAL-015). Ordinary module fees are verified by decoding the retained public client config.
